articles.title: ‘Everything you’d want from Italy, all in one place’: Brescia, Lombardy’s hidden gem
articles.summary: The city’s rich history and culture have so far flown under the radar, but its fiercely proud inhabitants are determined to change that. We have hardly begun walking before I spot the side alley, curving away from the main road in a patchwork of sunlit yellow walls, shuttered windows and shadowy…
body: I turn up the alley. There’s a lot of graffiti. Next to an anarchy symbol, someone has sprayed “ morte al decoro ” – death to decorum. I’m intrigued. We go further, finding a labyrinth of colourful streets filled with bars and restaurants, a few just opening up for the day.

Like the bohemian quarter at its heart, Brescia is an Italian city that is easily missed: it’s near the Dolomites and Lake Garda, but not close enough to be a base for them. Tourists tend to speed past on their way to Milan or Verona. Fiercely proud of her city, Elena is on a mission to convince me it is worth a stop. “You’ll see. We’ve got everything you’d want from Italy, all in one place.”

Her confidence is matched by Andrea, the manager of i Dù dela Contrada, a Carmine bar that we step into for a coffee. Quirky bric-a-brac is dotted around, the bar itself plastered with passport photos, donated by its many fans. “Twenty years ago, this was an area for prostitutes and thieves,” Andrea tells me. “Now it’s safer but still vibrant, and growing.”
I tell him Elena’s mission and he nods. “She’s right, ask anyone.”
points: The city’s rich history and culture have so far flown under the radar, but its fiercely proud inhabitants are determined to change that.

articles.title: A new start after 60: I became a grocer – and feel stronger physically and quieter mentally
articles.summary: Robert Solomon loves the early mornings, picking out the apples, tending to the broccoli and fussing up the dandelion greens. At 71, he says it’s the best job he’s had.
body: When Robert Solomon’s working hours were cut during the pandemic – he did building management and tech support for a nonprofit organisation – he got an extra job at a food cooperative, helping to stock the store. It was, he says, the most ordinary job, but that’s what made it special.

That job ended with the pandemic, but in 2022 he left the nonprofit and hunted for grocery positions. Now, at 71, he is assistant buyer in produce (ie fruit and vegetables) at an independent market in New York. “I love the opportunity to do physical, creative work with my body, hands and mind,” he says. “I’m working harder than I have since my 30s, and I love it.”

Solomon’s favourite time of day is the morning. He often starts at 5.30am or 6am. “I put the rugs back on the floor and the carts out in the yard. And then I start stocking.” Certain products make him particularly happy.

articles.title: Courgette kraut and fermented pepper sauce: Šárka Otevřel Camrdová’s Czech pickle recipes
articles.summary: In an extract from her new book, the Prague-born food writer shares two ways to preserve summer vegetables so they can be savoured year-round. Preserving the abundance of summer produce is a wonderful way to extend the season long after the gardens have faded.
body: This kraut can be used much like traditional sauerkraut, though its flavour is milder and its texture more delicate. Sauteed with onions in a little butter or lard, it makes an excellent accompaniment to roast meats and sausages; it can also be added to potato pancakes or used as a filling for savoury pies and pastries.
Wash the unpeeled courgettes and pat them dry. Cut the courgettes in half lengthways, scrape out the seeds and shred or coarsely grate the flesh into a bowl.

Mix the sugar, salt and vinegar, then pour this over the courgettes. Sprinkle in the caraway seeds, mix well and set aside for 15-30 minutes. Adjust the seasoning to taste, adding sugar or vinegar as required.

articles.title: I tested 15 pairs of women's running shoes over five months. These are my favorites for every type of surface and runner
articles.summary: Over five months, I evaluated shoes from On, Nike, Adidas, Hoka and more to find out which belong on your next road or trail run. The 13 best pairs of women’s shoes for the office, vetted by style professionals. Our top running essentials for beating the heat.
body: Finding the right running shoes is overwhelming if you’re not sure what to look for. Footwear can make or break your run, and there are a sea of options – from sleek carbon-plated racers to aggressive rubber-lugged trail runners.

As a lifelong athlete whose running ranges from holiday-themed 5Ks to trail races in the mountains, I’ve learned that footwear is the most important part of a runner’s gear setup. I am constantly looking for the best pair of shoes to help each run feel enjoyable.

To help other women find their perfect footwear match, I tested 15 pairs of the most highly rated women’s running shoes on the market to see which stood out above the rest. I took notes on cushion and impact absorption, weight, fit, breathability and other qualities. After many miles (over a variety of surfaces), winners were chosen in several categories.
Whether you have worn the same pair for years and are ready for an upgrade, or you have never run at all, we are here to help you choose the best women’s running shoes in 2026.

articles.title: Are Creators Up to the Task of Their New Marketing Roles?
articles.summary: The creator job description is no longer limited to making and distributing content — influencers are now expected to have business savvy to boot.
body: For over 70 years, the Cannes Lions festival has welcomed marketing and advertising suits to the South of France for a week of schmoozing and dealmaking. In recent years, though, a new crowd has descended on the French Riviera: influencers. And in 2026, they were front and center, speaking on panels, attending lunches, dinners and parties, and taking meetings along the Croisette.
For some, it was the farthest they’d gone into the business side of content marketing. Cannes may be a fabulous setting for a conference, but it’s a conference nonetheless.

For most influencers, they’ve built followings online because they’re funny or aspirational, not because of their business savvy. Now, brands more often want them to take on the role of representatives at industry events — and to contribute to marketing strategies back home.

“The role of an influencer/creator in 2026 looks very different from what it was,” says influencer marketing agency Ponte Firm founder Shana Davis. Caroline Wilson, an executive in UTA’s brand advisory group, refers to creators as “a marketing strategy” in and of themselves, as opposed to a prong or add-on in a larger marketing machine separate from them.
points: The creator job description is no longer limited to making and distributing content — influencers are now expected to have business savvy to boot.

articles.title: In Luxury’s New Resale Era, Everyone’s a Fashion Expert
articles.summary: The RealReal’s 2026 resale report illustrates the rise in specificity and saviness in luxury resale. This will change how the industry operates.
body: Gone are the days of simply searching names like “Prada” on resale sites and scrolling away. In 2026, shoppers are getting ultra-specific with their secondhand marketplace searches, a shift that has wider implications for the resale industry.

“The hyper-specificity of the way that people search really stands out as a fundamental shift in the way people think about shopping,” says Kristen Naiman, chief brand officer at luxury online resale marketplace The RealReal. “The fact that people are searching for not just ‘Prada 2010’, but ‘Prada 2010 linen’ or ‘Chanel 2013, look 31’ tells me they have developed both a fluency around style and fashion, as well as an emphasis on singularity and one-of-oneness.”

This was one of the key takeaways of The RealReal’s 2026 resale report, which takes stock of the biggest shifts and developments in the secondhand market. The root of the shift is two-pronged, Naiman says: people want more unique clothes, and they want to invest in items they can make a return from down the line. Forty-seven percent of shoppers actively evaluate an item’s potential resale value before making a purchase in the primary market.
points: The RealReal’s 2026 resale report illustrates the rise in specificity and saviness in luxury resale.

articles.title: How Sophie McIntosh Wrote ‘Benevolent,’ One of the Most Bracing Plays of the Year
articles.summary: The playwright speaks to Vogue about drawing inspiration from New York’s old reformatory homes, why she still believes in content warnings, and what it means for a play to be truly “political.”
body: Benevolent, the latest work from playwright Sophie McIntosh ( Macbitches ), tells the story of four young women at Inwood’s Benevolent Home—a reformatory house for fallen and friendless girls—in 1917. Directed by McIntosh’s longtime collaborator Nina Goodheart, the play’s action unfolds in a basement laundry room, where the wards endlessly scrub at the most sickeningly soiled sheets on their washboards, with more laundry coming down the chute, located at center stage, at regular intervals.

The four residents have found themselves in the Benevolent Home for different reasons. There is the spoiled, 17-year-old Abby (Livvy Marcus), the youngest; the far more mature Emma (Mia Fowler), a Black sex worker at a “50-cent joint”; the brash Margaret (Chani Reese), whose whiteness has afforded her work at some of the more lucrative $10 brothels; and Sarah (Rachel Ravel), the most buoyant of the bunch, who has been panhandling on the Coney Island Boardwalk (or “Sodom by the Sea,” as Abby has heard her father refer to it). Over the course of the play, we see the women confront challenging truths about themselves and each other, bridging the gaps in their ages and experience.
points: The playwright speaks to Vogue about drawing inspiration from New York’s old reformatory homes, why she still believes in content warnings, and what it means for a play to be truly “political.”

articles.title: 17 Dreamy Miami Airbnbs in South Beach, Wynwood, and Beyond
articles.summary: These standout properties feature sprawling pools, sleek amenities, and walkable addresses.
body: I’ve always liked Miami best with a little room to spread out. I grew up coming here on family vacations, then came back for solo escapes, girls’ trips, and romantic weekends by the beach. Somehow, I still find myself falling for the city’s distinct combination of pastel Art Deco buildings, swaying palm trees, warm ocean air, and vibrant neighborhoods that feel like their own little universes.

Hotels can of course be fabulous here, but there’s something especially fun about having your own Miami address for a few days. A Miami Airbnb gives you the space to make coffee in your pajamas, open the doors to a pool or garden, pile everyone onto a sofa after the beach, and actually unpack instead of living out of a suitcase. I’m talking a leafy Coconut Grove hideaway, a glossy Brickell apartment with skyline views, or a colorful family house with a pool that has the potential to make leaving for dinner feel like a chore.
These are the Airbnbs I'd genuinely want to stay at in Miami—from breezy beach bases to character-filled homes that make a weekend away feel like a proper escape.
